hero.headline: Circle vs Circle.so
hero.subheadline: A side-by-side comparison for buyers, operators, and affiliate-content readers.

summary.winner_hint: No major feature winner — choose by brand trust or buying path
summary.best_for_a: Best for creators and marketers who like a concise, marketable name when describing their community platform.
summary.best_for_b: Best for teams and organizations that prefer the official Circle identity and want documentation, billing, and support tied to the circle.so domain.
summary.quick_take: Circle and Circle.so point to the same community platform experience: threaded posts, spaces, events, membership gating, and integrations that large and small communities use. There’s no dramatic product gap — differences are primarily about branding, sign-up route, and perception. If you’re converting members or linking to your home for trust signals, the official circle.so domain can help. If you’re focused on messaging and concise wording in marketing, the shorter Circle name works fine. Pick the sign-up flow, plan, and support option that fits your budget and timeline.

paragraphs: Choosing between Circle and Circle.so can feel like splitting hairs — both names point to the same modern community platform used for cohorts, memberships, events, and discussion hubs. The right pick is less about missing features and more about how you present the product to members and where you sign up.

On this page we compare the two identities across branding, buying path, support, and other practical dimensions so you can confidently direct prospects, choose a billing route, and optimize conversion language for landing pages and affiliate links.

data.headline: Same core platform — choose by trust, pricing, or path to purchase

items.question: Are Circle and Circle.so different products?
items.answer: No — they refer to the same community platform. Differences are about branding, the sign-up path, and how billing/support are managed rather than core features.

items.question: Will community behavior or features differ if I use one name over the other?
items.answer: No. Members will have the same experience; posts, spaces, events, and membership rules work the same regardless of whether you reference Circle or circle.so.

items.question: Which should I use in marketing links and landing pages?
items.answer: Use circle.so when you want the official domain for trust and verification. Use Circle in headlines and short copy for cleaner phrasing. For links, prefer the official domain to reduce confusion.

items.question: How should I choose between them for my purchase?
items.answer: Compare plan details, trial offers, and support options. If enterprise billing, SLAs, or account management matter, sign up through the official circle.so path; if you’re optimizing copy or affiliate creatives, use the short Circle name for clarity.
